subject: GPU fleet sizing for multi-request patterns & packaging clarifications
messages:
From: Arjun Shah <arjun@helios-ai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask — mixed chat + batch embed workloads (Helios)

Hey Tessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We’re moving toward a committed Dedicated deployment and want a practical starting point for pool sizing and packaging. High level:

- Production chat (customer-facing): peak ~18 RPS sustained for short bursts up to 45 RPS (1–2 min).
- Avg chat context length: 1.2k tokens input, 1.0k tokens output. Model target: a 30B-style conversational model (we’ll evaluate quantized variants).
- Background embeddings: ~2k requests per hour, each 512-d embedding, non-latency-sensitive batch windows.
- KV cache hit expected ~25% on chat prefix reuse.

Questions:
1) How many GPUs do you recommend for a 3-year reserved commit to meet 99th %-ile latency SLO of <350ms tail for chat?
2) What commit tiers and discount frameworks do you offer for 12/24/36 month terms?
3) Any packaging tips to handle the bursty 45 RPS spikes without huge overcommit?

I attached a small sample of request traces (helios_workload_sample.csv). Would appreciate a ballpark and we can iterate.

Thanks,
Arjun
VP Engineering — Helios AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Shah <arjun@helios-ai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — mixed chat + batch embed workloads (Helios)

Hi Arjun —

Appreciate the context and the sample trace. I pulled Ben onto the thread; he owns Dedicated sizing. Quick initial notes before we dig into the CSV:

- For conversational workloads with ~1.2k in / 1.0k out we usually budget on effective tokens-per-request ~2.2k, and plan for KV cache to reduce compute per request by ~15–25% depending on reuse patterns.
- Spiky 45 RPS bursts are best handled with a small burst buffer + autoscale (warm standby GPUs) rather than full provision for sustained peak.
- Dedicated commit tiers: we can offer committed GPU-equivalent units (CEUs) and map to physical GPU counts for quoting. Discount depends on term + volume + model profile.

Ben — can you sketch a 1) conservative baseline pool, 2) a burst strategy, and 3) pricing/discount bands we should present (12/24/36)? Also helpful to call out quantization impact (FP16 vs 4-bit) on throughput & memory.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Arjun Shah <arjun@helios-ai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — mixed chat + batch embed workloads (Helios)

Arjun / Tessa —

Thanks for the trace. I did a short pass on the CSV and sketched three scenarios below. These are engine-level estimates (conservative) for a 30B-style model. Actual throughput will vary by model distillation/quantization and kernel selection.

Scenario A — Baseline (single-region, steady-state planning)- Target SLO: 99th <350ms for chat at steady loads- Sustained chat RPS: 18- Effective tokens/request: 2.2k (with 25% KV hit)- Recommended GPUs: 3 x H100-80GB equivalent (continuous serving)- Embeddings: colocate on same pool with low-priority lanes; embeddings load consumes ~0.2 GPU equivalent on average- Notes: With continuous batching and KV cache this setup gives headroom for modest growth (~x1.2)

Scenario B — Burst-handling + warm standby- SLO including short spikes to 45 RPS- Same sustained 18 RPS, spikes 45 RPS (1–2 min)- Recommended: 3 x H100 (active) + 1 x H100 warm standby (pre-warmed; autoscale to active for spikes)- Warm standby cost: lower than full active commit; recommend 20% extra commit for burst buffer + short-term overcommit policy

Scenario C — Aggressive quant + cost-optimized commit- Assume 4-bit quantization and optimized kernels (30–40% throughput uplift)- Sustained: 18 RPS handled by 2 x H100 equiv, spikes covered by 1 warm standby (total commit 3 CEUs)- Tradeoffs: potential small quality delta; need evals to confirm regression tolerance

Throughput math (quick):
- Single H100 equiv, conversational 30B FP16: ~8–12 chat RPS at 2.2k tokens w/ batching (est.)
- 3 GPUs -> ~24–36 RPS sustained depending on batching efficiency; 25% KV hit improves effective RPS by ~12–18%

Pricing / discount framework (ballpark, per-GPU-equivalent CEU):
- 12-month: list price (no term discount)
- 24-month: ~12% discount off list
- 36-month: ~18–22% discount + commit credits (one-time onboarding credit)
- Additional: volume tiers (>= 6 CEUs) unlocks an extra 6–8% off and priority capacity SLAs

Packaging tips:
- Recommend mapping to CEUs in the quote, and show 2 commit packages: "Baseline" (3 CEUs) and "Burst-ready" (4 CEUs with warm standby). Be explicit about autoscale cooldowns and burst policy.
- Allow Helios to start at 24-month commit with a 6-month ramp: first quarter at 60% of CEUs to reduce early cost friction.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short pricing PDF with examples and a sample Ramp & Autoscale policy.

If this looks good I can turn it into a formal quote; Laura can handle legal/terms and finalize discount bands.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups:

- Can you put CEU -> physical GPU mapping for us (eg. CEU 1 = H100-80GB, or 1.2 x A100-80GB if via cloud)? We’re comparing on-prem vs cloud prices.
- For the 24-month ramp (60% first quarter) do you have an example invoice/credit schedule? We need that to model cash flow for Finance.
- Any recommended guardrails for warm standby autoscale to avoid cold-start latency?

We want to prioritize predictability over absolute lowest cost, so the 24-month with a burst-ready option sounds like our preferred path.

Appreciate it — Arjun
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sizing ask — mixed chat + batch embed workloads (Helios)

Arjun —

Couple concrete items we’ll include in the quote package:

1) CEU mapping (for quoting clarity):
- 1 CEU = 1 H100-80GB physical GPU equivalent (reference). If customer wants A100 or A10 cloud mappings we provide a conversion table (example: 1 CEU ≈ 1.25 A100-80GB or 2.8 A10G depending on model profile).

2) Ramp & billing example (24-month):
- Month 1–3: bill at 60% of committed CEUs
- Month 4–12: bill at 90% of committed CEUs
- Month 13–24: bill at 100% committed CEUs
- Credits: applied as monthly amortized credit in months 1–6 to smooth ramp where applicable

3) Warm-standby guardrails:
- Keep 1 GPU pre-warmed (hot kernels loaded, model sharded) and maintain short-term token cache refresh policies to avoid large cold-starts
- Autoscale policy: immediate scale to add standby for bursts up to 2x sustained in <30s; scale to full active within 90s for multi-GPU adds (depends on model load time)

Next steps: I’ll generate a formal quote with the two packaging options (Baseline 3 CEUs, Burst-ready 4 CEUs) and a 24-month pricing column with the discount margin applied. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

-Laura
